blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Tiny object detection remains challenging because tiny instances occupy only a few pixels, and their fine-grained details are easily lost during feature downsampling. Although the highest-resolution feature preserves rich local details for tiny objects, DETR-like detectors often discard it due to its large computational cost, while directly reintroducing this feature also brings dense background noise. To address this problem, we propose ReDHF, a novel framework that Revives the Discarded High-resolution Feature for tiny object detection. ReDHF has three cooperative components. Cross-Scale Deformable Fusion (CSDF) first constructs a semantically enhanced highest-resolution feature and injects its fine-grained details into the shallow feature under a moderate cost. Ellipse-Guided Shallow Supervision (EGSS) then guides the enhanced feature to learn more reliable classification and localization priors by applying geometry-adaptive auxiliary supervision. Full-Scale Query Interaction (FSQI) further enables decoder queries to access both low-level details and high-level semantic information, allowing them to aggregate richer cues for tiny objects. Extensive experiments show that ReDHF consistently improves multiple baselines across different DETR variants and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the evaluated benchmarks. The best ReDHF variants surpass their baselines by +1.4 AP on AI-TOD-v2, +1.6 AP on VisDrone, and +1.5 AP on SODA-D, with especially notable gains on tiny and small objects.
blocks.zh: 细小的物体探测仍然具有挑战性,因为细小的事件只占据了少数像素,在特征下取样时,它们细微的纹理细节很容易丢失. 虽然最高分辨率的特性为细小物体保留了丰富的局部细节,但类似DETR的探测器经常因为巨大的计算成本而丢弃它,而直接重新引入这个特性也会带来密集的背景噪声. 为了解决这个问题,我们提出ReDHF,这个新颖的框架,将弃置的高分辨率特性用于微小物体的探测. REDHF有三个合作部分. 跨尺度变形融合(CSDF)首先构筑了精密增强的最高分辨率特征,并以中度成本将其精细细节注入浅层特征. 椭圆-guided Shallow监管(EGSS)然后通过应用几何适应辅助监管来指导增强的特征,以学习更可靠的分类和本地化前科. 全程查询交互(FSQI)进一步使解码器查询既可以访问低级细节,又可以访问高级语义信息,使得它们可以将更丰富的提示集合到微小对象上. 广泛的实验表明,REDHF不断改进不同DETR变体的多个基线,并实现评价基准的最新性能. 最好的ReDHF变体在AI-TOD-v2,+1.6 AP在VisDrone,+1.5 AP在SODA-D上超过了它们的基线,在微小物体上特别显著的收获.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Object detection has advanced rapidly, with both CNN-based detectors [ 7 , 9 , 12 , 20 , 27 , 31 , 34 , 35 , 41 , 44 ] and Transformer-based detectors [ 4 , 5 , 38 , 25 , 29 , 30 , 52 , 56 , 59 ] achieving strong performance. However, detecting tiny objects remains difficult, especially in aerial, remote sensing, and traffic scenarios. Tiny objects occupy only a few pixels, leaving their edges, textures, and geometric cues weak in the image and further weakened by feature downsampling. As a result, high-level features often fail to preserve sufficient discriminative details for tiny objects, as illustrated in Fig. 1 (b).
blocks.zh: 物体探测进展迅速,有CNN型探测器[7,9,12,20,27,31,34,35,41,44]和变形器型探测器[4,5,38,25,29,30,52,56,59]都取得了强效. 然而,探测小物体仍然困难重重,特别是在空中、遥感和交通方面。 细小的物体只占据了几像素,留下了边缘,纹理,和图像中的几何提示被弱化并被特征下采样所进一步削弱. 因此,如图1(b)所示,高层特征往往无法为小物体保留足够的歧视性细节。

blocks.en: To address the issues of tiny object detection, a natural idea is to preserve these weak cues by using higher-resolution inputs or features. Prior works have shown that high-resolution information is important for tiny objects. For example, Deformable DETR [ 59 ] points out that small objects rely on high-resolution feature maps, and DM-EFS [ 37 ] shows that shallower high-resolution features can improve tiny-object representation. However, many detectors [ 26 , 52 , 59 , 25 ] still discard the highest-resolution backbone feature to control computation. This design saves overhead but sacrifices the local details that are critical for tiny objects. As shown in Fig. 1 (a)(c), discarding this feature becomes especially detrimental on AI-TOD-v2 [ 46 ] , VisDrone [ 58 ] , and SODA-D [ 6 ] , where ultra-tiny objects with a short side no larger than 4 pixels appear frequently and may be compressed to nearly a single point even on a stride-4 feature map. Meanwhile, directly reintroducing the highest-resolution backbone feature is also impractical, since it has a much larger spatial size that may lead to unacceptable extra cost, and its shallow responses contain dense background activations that may overwhelm weak tiny-object signals. These issues highlight the pressing need for detection frameworks that can balance fine-grained information preservation with computational efficiency.
blocks.zh: 为了解决微小物体检测问题,一个自然的想法是通过使用高分辨率输入或特性来保留这些弱提示. 先前的作品已经表明高分辨信息对微小物体很重要. 例如可变形的DETR [59]指出,小物体依赖于高分辨率地物图,而DM-EFS [37] 显示更浅高分辨率地物可以改善小物体的表示. 然而,许多探测器[26,52,59,25]仍然抛弃了控制计算的最高分辨率主干线特性. 这种设计节省了间接费用,但牺牲了当地对小物体至关重要的细节。 如图1 (a)(c)所示,丢弃这一特性对AI-TOD-v2 [46],VisDrone [58],和SODA-D [6]特别不利,其中短边不大于4像素的超直线物体经常出现,甚至会被压缩到近一分,甚至会出现在出步-4特征图上. 同时,直接重新引入最高分辨率的主干道功能也是不切实际的,因为它的空间大小要大得多,可能导致不可接受的额外费用,而它的浅层反应包含密集的背景活化会压倒弱小物体信号. 这些问题突出表明迫切需要建立能够平衡精细信息保存与计算效率的检测框架。

blocks.en:
In this work, we propose ReDHF , a novel and efficient plug-and-play high-resolution detail reintroduction framework for Deformable-DETR-like detectors, which revives the discarded highest-resolution backbone feature while controlling computation and background disturbance through three cooperative components.
First, to address the contradiction between the limited representation of small objects and the high cost of utilizing high-resolution features, we design a lightweight Cross-Scale Deformable Fusion (CSDF) module that semantically enhances the highest-resolution feature to provide more useful fine-grained cues with moderate cost. Second, considering that high-resolution features mainly include low-level edges and textures and are more likely to introduce background noise, we apply Ellipse-Guided Shallow Supervision (EGSS) to guide the shallow feature to learn more stable classification and localization priors. Moreover, since final predictions in DETR-like detectors are query-driven, we further propose Full-Scale Query Interaction (FSQI) , which integrates the semantically enhanced highest-resolution feature together with higher-level features into the encoder memory, so that decoder queries can directly access pixel-level details and improve their ability of detecting tiny objects. Overall, ReDHF makes more effective use of the highest-resolution backbone feature with only a modest extra cost and significantly improves tiny object detection.
blocks.zh:
在这部作品中,我们提出ReDHF,一个全新的高效插座和游戏高分辨率细节再引入可变形-DETR型探测器的再引入框架,它重振被丢弃的最高分辨率主干功能,同时通过三个合作部分控制计算和背景扰动.
首先,为了解决小物体代表性有限与使用高分辨率特性成本高之间的矛盾,我们设计了一个轻量级可变形聚变(CSDF)模块,该模块集成地增强最高分辨率特性,以提供更有用的有中度成本的精细分量的提示. 其次,考虑到高分辨特征主要包括低等边缘和纹理并更可能引入背景噪声,我们采用"椭圆-Guided Shallow Conference"(EGSS)来引导浅层特征学习更稳定的分类和本地化前科. 此外,由于DETR-类似探测器中的最后预测是查询驱动的,我们进一步提出"全程查询相互作用"(FSQI),将精密增强的最高分辨率特性与更高级的特性结合到编码器内存中,这样解码器查询就可以直接访问像素级的细节并提高其探测出细小物体的能力. 总体而言,REDHF更有效地利用了最高分辨率的骨干特性,只增加了少量的额外成本,并大大改进了微小物体的探测.

blocks.en: Extensive experiments show that ReDHF consistently improves multiple DETR-like [ 52 , 59 , 14 ] baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance. Specifically, the best ReDHF model achieves 35.7% AP on AI-TOD-v2 [ 46 ] , improving AP vt to 20.8% (+1.2%) over its corresponding baseline. In addition, the ReDHF variant built upon DINO-4scale [ 52 ] reduces GFLOPs by 86.7% compared with directly integrating the highest-resolution feature, as detailed in Appendix D . On VisDrone [ 58 ] and SODA-D [ 6 ] , ReDHF again brings consistent gains. The best ReDHF model achieves 40.6% AP and 38.7% AP, and also improves AP s to 33.1% (+1.6%) and AP eS to 21.4% (+1.7%), respectively. These results support our claim that the highest-resolution feature, though often discarded for efficiency, can be effectively revived through semantic enhancement. In summary, our main contributions are:

blocks.en: • We revisit the commonly discarded highest-resolution backbone feature in DETR-like detectors and show that its effective reuse requires addressing not only computational cost, but also weak semantics and noisy shallow responses. • We propose ReDHF, which revives the discarded feature through semantically enhanced highest-resolution feature construction (CSDF), training-time shallow auxiliary supervision (EGSS), and decoder full-scale query interaction (FSQI), thereby enabling efficient high-resolution detail reintroduction for tiny-object detection. • We validate ReDHF on multiple DETR-like baselines across AI-TOD-v2, VisDrone, and SODA-D. It achieves state-of-the-art performance and consistently improves the baselines with average gains of +1.5 AP vt , +1.7 AP s , and +1.8 AP eS on the three datasets, respectively.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Tiny object detection
blocks.zh: 2.1 国家 微小对象检测

blocks.en: Identifying tiny objects is inherently difficult because tiny instances provide limited visual evidence and are vulnerable to complex background noise. Early CNN-based detectors, such as Faster R-CNN [ 9 , 35 ] , often struggle with such objects due to inadequate feature representation and limited context modeling. Some works improve tiny-object learning by enriching training samples, such as copy-pasting augmentation [ 18 ] and instance-level transformations [ 60 ] . Recently, transformer-based models [ 4 , 19 , 25 , 30 , 38 , 52 , 56 , 59 ] have shown strong potential by bypassing hand-crafted post-processing like NMS and leveraging self-attention mechanisms. Cross-DINO [ 3 ] combines deep MLP representations with transformer encoder features through a Cross Coding Twice Module to enhance small-object details. DQ-DETR [ 15 ] introduces density maps to adjust query numbers and positions based on instance density, while Dome-DETR [ 14 ] further improves tiny object detection by generating density-oriented features. However, these methods often rely heavily on specific density modeling or carefully designed query mechanisms, which may complicate the optimization process and limit their flexibility across different datasets.
blocks.zh: 微小物体的识别本身就很困难,因为微小的例子提供了有限的视觉证据并容易受到复杂的背景噪声的影响. 早期基于CNN的探测器,如更快速的R-CNN [9,35],由于地物表现不足和上下文模型制作有限等原因,经常与这类物体相争. 一些作品通过丰富培训样本来改进小对象学习,如复制-粘贴增强[18]和实例级转换[60]. 最近,以变压器为主的型号[4,19,25,30,38,52,56,59]通过绕过NMS等手动后处理,并发挥自留机制的杠杆作用,显示出了强大的潜力. Cross-DINO [3]通过一个Cross Coding Twice Module将MLP深层的表示与变压器编码器特性结合,来增强小对象细节. DQ-DETR [15]引入了密度图来根据实例密度来调整查询数字和位置,而Dome-DETR [14] 则通过生成以密度为导向的特征来进一步改善微小物体的探测. 然而,这些方法往往严重依赖特定的密度模型或精心设计的查询机制,这可能会使优化过程复杂化并限制它们在不同数据集上的灵活性.

blocks.en: 2.2 Multi-scale and high-resolution features
blocks.zh: 2.2 多尺度高分辨率特性

blocks.en: Feature pyramids [ 20 ] are widely used to handle object scale variation. Advanced architectures like BiFPN [ 40 ] and DetectoRS [ 32 ] , improve cross-level information flow through bidirectional fusion or recursive feedback. For tiny objects, fusion factors [ 10 ] further regulate adjacent pyramid levels to reduce the learning burden. Recent works also explore high-resolution information more explicitly. QueryDet [ 49 ] refines sparse locations from low to high resolutions. ESOD [ 24 ] uses patch slicing and sparse prediction to reduce redundant computation on high-resolution features. DM-EFS [ 37 ] expands feature sets to enrich small-object representations. These works show the value of high-resolution cues for tiny objects. However, many detection pipelines still discard the highest-resolution backbone feature to keep computation affordable, leaving the finest local details underused. In contrast, our method revives this discarded feature through semantic enhancement, making its fine-grained details more compatible and usable for tiny object detection.
blocks.zh: 地物金字塔 [20]被广泛用于处理对象尺度变化. BiFPN [40]和DetectoRS [32]等高级架构,通过双向聚变或递归反馈来改进跨级信息流. 对于细小的物体,聚变因子[10]进一步调节相邻的金字塔水平来减轻学习负担. 最近的工作还更明确地探索高分辨率信息。 QueryDet [49] 从低分辨率到高分辨率细化了稀有位置. ESOD [24] 使用补丁切片和稀有预测来减少高分辨率特性上冗余计算. DM-EFS [37] 扩展了功能集来丰富小对象表达. 这些作品展现出高分辨率提示对小物体的价值. 然而,许多探测管道仍然丢弃了最高分辨率的主干线功能,以保持可承受的计算能力,使当地最好的细节没有得到充分利用。 相比之下,我们的方法通过语义增强使这个被丢弃的特性复活,使其精细的纹理细节更加相容并可用于微小物体检测.

blocks.en: 2.3 Auxiliary supervision and label assignment
blocks.zh: 2.3 辅助监督和标签分配

blocks.en: Auxiliary supervision has been widely used to strengthen intermediate representations in object detection. In CNN-based detectors, DSFPN [ 50 ] , LAF-YOLOv10 [ 8 ] and Jin et al. [ 16 ] attach auxiliary prediction heads to early backbone stages or bottom-up pathways to improve feature learning. A similar idea is adopted in DETR-like models [ 52 , 15 , 14 , 30 , 38 ] , where auxiliary losses on intermediate decoder layers are commonly used to stabilize training and facilitate optimization. Beyond intermediate decoder supervision, MLP-DINO [ 2 ] introduces query-independent category supervision to mitigate the sensitivity of category predictions to bounding box prediction.
blocks.zh: 辅助监督被广泛用于加强物体探测中的中间能表示. 在以CNN为基础的探测器中,DSFPN [50],LAF-YOLOv10 [8]和Jin等. [16] 附加辅助预测头到早期骨干阶段或自下而上路径来改进特征学习. 类似DETR的型号 [52, 15, 14, 30, 38] 中也采用了类似的想法,其中中间解码器层的辅助损失通常被用来稳定训练和便利优化. 除了中间解码器监督之外,MLP-DINO [2]引入了查询-独立类别监督,以降低类别预测对边框预测的敏感性.

blocks.en: Label assignment is another key factor affecting detection performance. ATSS [ 53 ] shows that positive and negative sample definitions are critical. For generic object detection, AutoAssign [ 57 ] and IQDet [ 28 ] select high-quality regions according to predicted quality scores, while FCOS [ 43 ] formulates detection as dense per-pixel prediction. For transformer-based detectors, DS-Det [ 11 ] introduces a unified Single-Query paradigm and disentangles cross-attention-based box localization with one-to-many assignment from self-attention-based deduplication with one-to-one assignment. However, tiny objects make assignment more difficult because small localization shifts can strongly affect matching quality. Recent methods therefore redesign assignment for tiny objects. UGS [ 39 ] shows that IoU-based assignment can be unstable for tiny objects and proposes a classification-based objective. DCNet [ 55 ] uses dynamic scale-aware assignment, while RFLA [ 47 ] matches Gaussian receptive fields with ground truth to alleviate positive-sample scarcity. Unlike these methods that mainly design assignment for final prediction, our work focuses on strengthening intermediate representations. Specifically, we propose a geometry-adaptive assignment strategy and auxiliary supervision to build coarse classification and localization priors for tiny objects, while the auxiliary head is removed during inference.
blocks.zh: 标签分配是影响检测性能的另一个关键因素. ATSS [53] 显示正和负的样本定义至关重要. 对于通用对象检测,AutoAssign [57]和IQDet [28]根据预测的质量分数选择了高质量的区域,而FCOS [43]则将检测表述为密集的每像素预测. 对于基于变压器的探测器,DS-Det[11]引入了统一的"单一查询"范式并分解出"交叉查询"的箱位本地化,从自留式分解中分解出"一对多"的"一对多". 然而,细小的物体使得分配更加困难,因为小的本地化转变会强烈地影响匹配的质量. 因此,最近的方法重新设计了小物体的任务。 UGS [39] 显示以IoU为基础的任务对于小对象来说可能不稳定,并提出了以分类为基础的目标. DCNet [55] 使用动态的有分级意识的任务,而RFLA [47] 则将高斯人接受球场与地面真理相匹配来缓解正样本稀缺. 与这些主要为最终预测设计任务的方法不同,我们的工作重点是加强中间表述。 具体来说,我们提出了一个几何适应性分配策略和辅助监督,为小物体构建粗细的分类和本地化前科,而辅助头则在推论中被取出.

blocks.en: Given an input image, let { C i } i = 1 l \{C_{i}\}_{i=1}^{l} denote the multi-level backbone features, and let { P i } i = 1 l \{P_{i}\}_{i=1}^{l} denote the corresponding multi-scale features after encoder context modeling, where C 1 C_{1} is the highest-resolution feature. To revive the discarded highest-resolution feature without incurring excessive computation or amplifying background responses, we propose ReDHF , a plug-and-play framework for transformer-based tiny object detection. As shown in Fig. 2 , ReDHF consists of three components: Cross-Scale Deformable Fusion (CSDF, Sec. 3.2 ), Ellipse-Guided Shallow Supervision (EGSS, Sec. 3.3 ), and Full-Scale Query Interaction (FSQI, Sec. 3.4 ). During training, CSDF and FSQI are optimized end-to-end in the main detection pipeline, while EGSS supervises the shallow feature to learn stable classification and localization priors. During inference, EGSS is completely removed, and only CSDF and FSQI remain for feature construction and decoder interaction.
blocks.zh: 在输入图像的情况下,让 { C i } i = 1 l = { C _{i i = 1} 表示多级主干功能,让{Pi}i = 1 l \{P_{i}\}_{i=i=1}^{l}表示编码器上下文建模后相应的多级功能,其中C 1 C_{1}为最高解析功能. 为了在不发生过多计算或扩大背景反应的情况下恢复已丢弃的最高分辨率特性,我们建议使用ReDHF,作为变压器微小物体探测的插件和播放框架。 如图2所示,REDHF由三个部分组成: 跨尺度可变同化(CSDF, 第3.2节),椭圆-导火索监督(EGSS, 第3.3节),和全尺度查询相互作用(FSQI, 第3.4节)。 在训练期间,CSDF和FSQI在主探测管被优化为端到端,而EGSS则监督浅接特征来学习稳定的分类和本地化前科. 在推论期间,EGSS被完全去除,只有CSDF和FSQI仍然用于地物构造和解码器交互.

blocks.en: 3.2 Cross-scale deformable fusion
blocks.zh: 3.2 跨尺度变形聚变

blocks.en: CSDF is designed to exploit the fine-grained details of the highest-resolution backbone feature while reducing the side effect of its noisy background responses. Instead of directly using raw C 1 C_{1} , CSDF first constructs a semantically enhanced highest-resolution feature P 1 P_{1} , and then injects its high-resolution details into the shallow feature P 2 P_{2} .
blocks.zh: CSDF旨在利用高分辨率骨干特性的精细细节,同时减少其噪音背景反应的副作用. CSDF没有直接使用生C 1 C_{1},而是首先构建出一个精密增强的最高分辨率特性P 1 P_{1},再将高分辨率的细节注入浅色特性P 2 P_{2}.

blocks.en: Directly using C 1 C_{1} is suboptimal because it contains rich details but weak semantics [ 20 ] , making it sensitive to background noises. To address this issue, we inject the semantic information from P 2 P_{2} into C 1 C_{1} through a lightweight RepNCSPELAN4 block [ 30 ] . Since lower layers preserve local details while higher layers aggregate more global context [ 33 ] , we only upsample P 2 P_{2} and fuse it with the projected C 1 C_{1} as follows: P 1 = ℱ RepNCSPELAN4 ​ ( Concat ⁡ ( Up ⁡ ( P 2 ) , ϕ ⁡ ( C 1 ) ) ) , P_{1}=\mathcal{F}_{\text{RepNCSPELAN4}}\big(\mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{Up}(P_{2}),\phi(C_{1}))\big), (1) where ϕ ⁡ ( ⋅ ) \phi(\cdot) denotes channel projection and ℱ RepNCSPELAN4 \mathcal{F}_{\text{RepNCSPELAN4}} denotes the fusion block. In this way, P 1 P_{1} preserves the high-resolution local details of C 1 C_{1} while inheriting the semantic prior from P 2 P_{2} , alleviating the semantic gaps between different depth features.

Since P ^ 1 \hat{P}_{1} is essentially local detail responses from P 1 P_{1} , it cannot replace the original P 2 P_{2} . blocks.en: 3.3 Ellipse-guided shallow supervision
blocks.zh: 3.3 椭圆制导浅层监督

blocks.en: EGSS aims to guide P 2 ′ P_{2}^{\prime} to learn reliable foreground classification and coarse localization priors, rather than making final predictions on the intermediate representation. Although CSDF enriches P 2 ′ P_{2}^{\prime} with high-resolution details, it may also transfer dense background responses from P 1 P_{1} to P 2 P_{2} . As shown in Fig. 4 , both P 1 P_{1} and P 2 P_{2} can respond strongly to background textures and local patterns. When injecting detail cues from P 1 P_{1} into P 2 P_{2} , these background responses may be transferred together with object-related details, thereby amplifying non-object responses in complex scenes. To address this side effect, we introduce EGSS, which applies shallow auxiliary supervision to P 2 ′ P_{2}^{\prime} during training and is completely removed during inference, introducing no additional inference cost.
blocks.zh: EGSS旨在指导P2 ' P_{2}^{\prime'学习可靠的前地分类和粗糙的本地化前事,而不是对中间代表进行最后预测. 虽然CSDF以高分辨率的细节丰富了P2'P_{2}^{\pprippripmeme},但它也可能将密集的背景响应从P1 P_{1}转移到P2 P_{2}. 如图4所示,P 1 P_{1}和P 2 P_{2}都可以对背景纹理和当地图案做出强烈反应. 当从P 1 P% 1} 插入到P 2 P% 2} 时, 这些背景响应可以连同与对象相关的细节一起转移,从而在复杂的场景中扩展非对象响应. 为了解决这一副作用,我们引入了EGSS,它在训练期间对P2 ' P_{2}^{\pprippripmeme'应用了浅的辅助监督,在推论期间被完全去除,没有引入额外的推论费用.

blocks.en: Standard FCOS-style dense supervision [ 43 ] usually adopts box-shaped assignment or fixed-radius center sampling, which is not ideal for tiny objects. Since tiny objects occupy only a few pixels, box boundaries often include background pixels and introduce noisy supervision. Center sampling can reduce boundary noise, but a fixed region cannot adapt well to different aspect ratios and may even remove all valid positives for extremely tiny objects.
blocks.zh: 标准的FCOS式密集监督[43]通常采用箱形任务或固定辐射中心采样,这对小物体来说并不理想. 由于微小的物体只占据了少数像素,所以箱形边界往往包括了背景像素并引入了吵闹的监管. 中心采样可以减少边界噪声,但固定区域不能很好地适应不同的侧相比,甚至可以去除极小物体的所有有效正数.

blocks.en: At the same time, the detail-enhanced shallow feature P 2 ′ P_{2}^{\prime} has a limited receptive field and is more suitable for detecting small objects. For large objects, a feature point on P 2 ′ P_{2}^{\prime} often perceives only a small part of the instance and cannot understand the complete structure well. Assigning such objects to supervise P 2 ′ P_{2}^{\prime} may introduce ambiguous signals and distract the shallow feature from tiny-object regions. Motivated by the scale-aware design of FCOS [ 43 ] , we restrict EGSS to size-matched objects and define positive samples with a scale filtering strategy and an ellipse-guided geometric constraint. blocks.en: Tiny-object regression is naturally sensitive to small localization shifts [ 39 ] , especially on noisy shallow features. Since P 2 ′ P_{2}^{\prime} still contains non-negligible background responses, as shown in Fig. 4 , a strong regression loss may force the auxiliary branch to fit unstable box targets and disturb foreground discrimination. We therefore assign a small regression weight. In addition, we do not adopt centerness supervision by default, since tiny objects have only a few valid locations on the feature map and their centerness targets can vary sharply and become unreliable on the noisy shallow feature. EGSS therefore focuses on foreground classification and coarse localization, while final box refinement is left to the decoder. We empirically validate this design choice in Appendix G.6 .
blocks.zh: Tiny-object回归自然对小局部化转动有敏感性[39],特别是在吵闹的浅层地貌上. 如图4所示,由于P2 ' P_{2 ' }^{\p}^{\pprime}仍然包含不可忽略的背景反应,严重的回归损失可能迫使辅助分支适应不稳定的盒子目标并扰动前缘歧视. 因此,我们分配了一个小的回归权重。 此外,我们不默认采用中心性监督,因为小物体在地物图上只有几个有效的位置,它们的中心性目标可以剧烈地变化,在吵闹的浅层地物上变得不可靠. 因此,EGSS专注于前地分级和粗细的本地化,而最终的箱型精细化则留给解码器. 我们在附录G.6中以经验验证了这一设计选择。

blocks.en: 3.4 Full-scale query interaction
blocks.zh: 3.4 全面查询互动

blocks.en: In DETR-like detectors [ 4 , 59 , 25 ] , final predictions are generated by decoder queries. Instead of attending only to high-level features, FSQI enables these queries to directly access the fine-grained details in P 1 P_{1} , further improving tiny object detection performance. Here, “full-scale” means that the decoder can attend to all feature levels, from the highest-resolution P 1 P_{1} to deeper semantic features.
blocks.zh: 在类似DETR的探测器[4,59,25]中,最终预测由解码器查询生成. FSQI不只关注高层次的特性,而是让这些查询能够直接访问P 1 PQQ1}中的精细细节,进一步提高了微小物体检测性能. 在这里,"全尺寸"是指解码器可以处理所有地物级别,从最高分辨率的P 1 P_{1}到更深层次的语义特征.

blocks.en: We flatten and concatenate the semantically enhanced highest-resolution feature P 1 P_{1} , the detail-enhanced shallow feature P 2 ′ P_{2}^{\prime} , and the higher-level features { P 3 , … , P l } \{P_{3},\dots,P_{l}\} to construct the full-scale encoder memory: ℳ = Concat ⁡ ( Flatten ⁡ ( P 1 ) , Flatten ⁡ ( P 2 ′ ) , … , Flatten ⁡ ( P l ) ) . \mathcal{M}=\mathrm{Concat}\big(\mathrm{Flatten}(P_{1}),\mathrm{Flatten}(P_{2}^{\prime}),\dots,\mathrm{Flatten}(P_{l})\big). (6) Here, ℳ \mathcal{M} serves as the value tokens for decoder cross-attention. Since P 1 P_{1} is semantically enhanced from raw C 1 C_{1} , its tokens are more compatible with the encoded features { P 3 , … , P l } \{P_{3},\dots,P_{l}\} , alleviating the distribution gap between different-level features. To avoid noisy shallow responses disturbing query selection, FSQI excludes P 1 P_{1} from query initialization and exposes it only during decoder cross-attention, where decoder queries can adaptively retrieve relevant high-resolution details.

blocks.en: Since the receptive field of P 1 P_{1} is relatively small, if we keep its sampling setting the same as other feature levels, decoder queries may fail to collect enough information from P 1 P_{1} . We therefore allocate more sampling points on P 1 P_{1} in decoder deformable cross-attention phase. In practice, FSQI increases the number of sampling points on P 1 P_{1} from 4 to 8, while keeping it unchanged for the remaining feature levels. This gives queries a larger local search radius on P 1 P_{1} and improves their access to fine-grained spatial cues for tiny object detection.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4个实验

blocks.en: 4.1 Datasets and evaluation metrics
blocks.zh: 4.1 数据集和评价衡量标准

blocks.en: We evaluate ReDHF on three challenging tiny-object detection datasets: AI-TOD-v2 [ 46 ] , VisDrone [ 58 ] , and SODA-D [ 6 ] . AI-TOD-v2 and VisDrone cover dense aerial scenes with many tiny instances, while SODA-D provides high-resolution traffic scenes with many small and extremely small objects. These datasets cover both aerial and driving scenarios, making them suitable for evaluating the generality of ReDHF. Detailed dataset statistics are provided in Appendix B .
blocks.zh: 我们用三个具有挑战性的微小物体探测数据集来评价ReDHF:AI-TOD-v2 [46],VisDrone [58],和SODA-D [6]. AI-TOD-v2和VisDrone覆盖了密集的空中场景,有许多极小的场景,而SODA-D则提供了高分辨率的交通场景,有许多小而极小的物体. 这些数据组既包括空中情况,也包括驾驶情况,因此适合评估REDHF的通用性. 详细数据集统计数据见附录B。

blocks.en: We use Average Precision (AP) [ 21 ] as the main metric, which is calculated as the mean AP over the range of IoU thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, with an interval of 0.05. To better evaluate performance on tiny objects, we also report dataset-specific scale-aware metrics. For AI-TOD-v2 [ 46 ] , we follow [ 45 ] and report AP vt , AP t , AP s , and AP m . For VisDrone [ 58 ] and SODA-D [ 6 ] , we report AP s and AP eS as the tiny-object metrics, respectively. Full scale-aware metrics are provided in Appendix C .
blocks.zh: 我们使用"平均精度"(AP)[21]作为主要度量衡,该度量衡被计算为IoU阈值范围从0.50到0.95的"平均精度". 为了更好地评价微小物体的性能,我们还报告了数据集特有的有尺度意识的度量衡。 对于AI-TOD-v2 [46],我们跟着[45],并报告AP vt,AP t,AP s,和AP m. 对于VisDrone [58]和SODA-D [6],我们分别将AP s和AP eS作为小对象的度量. 附录C提供了全比例尺度的衡量标准。

blocks.en: 4.2 Implementation details
blocks.zh: 4.2 执行细节

blocks.en: We evaluate ReDHF on three representative baselines: DINO-4scale [ 52 ] , DQ-DETR [ 15 ] , and Dome-DETR [ 14 ] . Dome-DETR uses HGNetv2 [ 56 ] as the backbone, while DINO-4scale and DQ-DETR use ResNet-50 [ 13 ] . All experiments are trained end-to-end and evaluated on 4 Tesla V100 GPUs. Unless otherwise stated, we keep all the baseline architectures unchanged and only introduce the three components of our method. For Dome-DETR and DQ-DETR, we follow their original configurations on AI-TOD-v2 and VisDrone. Since SODA-D is not included in their original benchmarks, we reuse the VisDrone training configuration for this dataset. For DINO-4scale, we adopt its default COCO [ 21 ] 24-epoch training recipe for all three datasets, changing only dataset-specific settings. For EGSS, we set r min = 0 r_{\min}=0 for all datasets, with r max = 8 r_{\max}=8 for AI-TOD-v2 and r max = 16 r_{\max}=16 for VisDrone and SODA-D. Complete training and implementation details are provided in Appendix A .
blocks.zh: 我们从三个具有代表性的基线对ReDHF进行评估:DINO-4级[52]、DQ-DETR [15]和Dome-DETR [14]。 Dome-DETR使用HGNetv2 [56]作为主干,而DINO-4scale和DQ-DETR则使用ResNet-50 [13]. 所有实验都经过了端到端的训练,并在4个特斯拉V100GPU上进行了评价. 除非另有说明,否则我们保持所有基线建筑不变,只引入我们方法的三个组成部分。 对于Dome-DETR和DQ-DETR,我们遵循他们在AI-TOD-v2和VisDrone上的原始配置. 由于SODA-D不包含在他们的原始基准中,我们重新使用此数据集的VisDrone训练配置. 对于DINO-4scale,我们采用默认的COCO[21]24-epoc培训配方,用于所有三个数据集,只改变数据集的特定设置. 对于EGSS,我们为所有数据集设定 r min = 0 r _{\min}=0,其中 r 最大 = 8 r_{\max}=8 为 AI-TOD-v2, r 最大 = 16 r_{\max}=16 为 VisDrone 和 SODA-D。 完整的培训和实施细节见附录A。

blocks.en: 4.3 Main results
blocks.zh: 4.3 主要成果

blocks.en: Table 1 reports the results on the AI-TOD-v2 [ 46 ] test split. ReDHF consistently improves all evaluated DETR-like variants, with average gains of +1.1 AP and +1.5 AP vt . Dome-DETR-L w/ ReDHF achieves the best result of 35.7 AP, surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods. The improvement is more notable on very tiny objects, with an average gain of +1.5 AP vt across the three baseline variants. ReDHF brings consistent gains for most metrics except for AP s or AP m , which is expected since medium objects rely less on fine-grained local details and can already be well represented by deeper semantic features.

blocks.en: 4.4 Efficiency analysis
blocks.zh: 4.4 效率分析

blocks.en: ReDHF aims to improve tiny object detection with moderate overhead. As shown in Table 1 , it consistently improves DETR-like baselines with limited increases in model size and computation. For example, on Dome-DETR-S [ 14 ] , ReDHF improves AP by +1.4 while just increasing the average GFLOPs from 173.1 to 188.2. Similar trends are observed on DINO-4scale [ 52 ] , DQ-DETR [ 15 ] , and other Dome-DETR variants. Appendix D provides a detailed complexity analysis.
blocks.zh: ReDHF旨在用中度高空改进微小物体探测. 如表1所示,它不断改进类似DETR的基线,在模型大小和计算方面略有增加。 例如,在Dome-DETR-S[14]上,REDHF将AP改进为+1.4,同时将平均GFLOP从173.1提高到188.2. 在DINO-4scale [52], DQ-DETR [15],以及其他Dome-DETR变体上也观察到了类似的趋势. 附 录 D提供了详细的复杂性分析。

blocks.en: Table 5 reports the contribution of each component. For CSDF, raw C 1 C_{1} reduces AP from 32.1 to 31.1, while the semantically aligned P 1 P_{1} improves AP to 32.7, indicating that raw high-resolution details suffer from background responses and semantic mismatch. For FSQI, adding raw C 1 C_{1} to the encoder memory improves AP to 32.5 since decoder queries can selectively attend to useful high-resolution details and are therefore less sensitive to shallow noise, and replacing it with P 1 P_{1} further improves AP to 32.8. In contrast, using P 1 P_{1} for query initialization drops AP to 31.9, suggesting that shallow high-resolution features are unsuitable for initializing decoder queries. When cooperating CSDF and FSQI together, AP can increase to 33.1, and EGSS further improves the full model to 33.5 AP and 18.9 AP vt , confirming the complementary effects of all components.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we propose ReDHF, a plug-and-play framework that revives the discarded highest-resolution feature for tiny object detection. Motivated by the contradiction between the limited representation of tiny objects and the high cost of utilizing high-resolution features, we introduce CSDF, EGSS, and FSQI to effectively address these issues, achieving consistent improvements across different DETR-like models on the AI-TOD-v2, VisDrone and SODA-D datasets.
Although retaining the highest-resolution representation introduces additional computation, ReDHF yields consistent gains that are most pronounced on tiny objects, and we only observe localized degradation for large objects in dense scenes with smaller-capacity variants. Detailed analyses are provided in Appendix F . Future work will explore more adaptive high-resolution feature utilization under low-resource and crowded scenes. We hope ReDHF can inspire continued progress in this area.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们提出ReDHF,一个插件和游戏框架,它复活了被丢弃的用于微小物体检测的最高分辨率特性. 受微小物体代表性有限与使用高分辨率特性成本相矛盾的驱使,我们引入了CSDF,EGSS,和FSQI来有效解决这些问题,实现AI-TOD-v2,VisDrone和SODA-D数据集上不同DETR类模型的一致改进.
虽然保留最高分辨率的表示法引入了额外的计算,但REDHF产生的持续收益在微小物体上最为显著,我们只观察到大物体在容量较小的变体的密集场景中的局部退化. 详细分析见附录F。 今后的工作将探索在资源匮乏和拥挤的场景下更适应性高分辨率的地物利用。 我们希望布隆迪国防军能够激励在这一领域继续取得进展。

blocks.en: We evaluate ReDHF on three representative DETR-based detectors: DINO-4scale [ 52 ] , DQ-DETR [ 15 ] , and Dome-DETR [ 14 ] . Dome-DETR adopts HGNetv2 [ 56 ] as its backbone, while DINO-4scale and DQ-DETR use ResNet-50 [ 13 ] . All experiments are trained end-to-end and evaluated on 4 Tesla V100 GPUs. Unless otherwise stated, we keep all the baseline architectures unchanged and only introduce the three components of our method.
blocks.zh: 我们用三个具有代表性的DETR探测器对REDHF进行评估:DINO-4scale [52],DQ-DETR [15],和Dome-DETR [14]. Dome-DETR采用HGNetv2 [56]作为其骨干,而DINO-4scale和DQ-DETR则使用ResNet-50 [13]. 所有实验都经过了端到端的训练,并在4个特斯拉V100GPU上进行了评价. 除非另有说明,否则我们保持所有基线建筑不变,只引入我们方法的三个组成部分。

blocks.en: AI-TOD-v2 [ 46 ] contains 28,036 aerial images with 752,745 annotated object instances. The dataset is split into 11,214 training images, 2,804 validation images, and 14,018 test images. It is characterized by extremely small object sizes, with an average object size of only 12.7 pixels. In particular, 86% of the objects are smaller than 16 pixels, and the largest object does not exceed 64 pixels. The object density also varies greatly across images, ranging from 1 to 2,667 objects per image, with an average of 24.64 and a standard deviation of 63.94.
blocks.zh: AI-TOD-v2 [46] 包含28,036个航空图像,并有752,745个附加注释的物体实例. 数据集分为11,214个训练图像,2,804个验证图像,14,018个测试图像. 其特点是物体尺寸极小,平均物体尺寸只有12.7像素. 特别是86%的物体都小于16像素,最大的物体不超过64像素. 不同图像的物体密度也相差很大,从每个图像的1到2,667个物体不等,平均为24.64个,标准偏差为63.94个.

blocks.en: VisDrone [ 58 ] contains 14,018 images across 10 distinct categories, with 6,471 images for training, 548 for validation, and 3,190 for testing. It covers diverse objects such as pedestrians, bicycles, and vehicles, and presents severe challenges in terms of diverse crowd densities. Specifically, the average number of objects per image is 40.7, with a standard deviation of 46.41.
blocks.zh: VisDrone [58] 包含14,018个图像,分为10个不同类别,其中6,471个图像用于培训,548个图像用于验证,3,190个图像用于测试. 它涵盖行人、自行车和车辆等各种物体,在不同的人群密度方面提出了严峻挑战。 具体而言,每个图像的平均对象为40.7个,标准偏差为46.41个.

blocks.en: SODA-D [ 6 ] contains 24,828 high-quality traffic-scene images with 278,433 annotated instances across 9 categories. The training, validation, and test subsets are split with an approximate ratio of 50% : 20% : 30%. The dataset includes high-resolution driving scenes with many small and extremely small objects under diverse real-world conditions, including different viewpoints, weather, and illumination. These properties make SODA-D a challenging benchmark for small object detection in driving scenarios.
blocks.zh: SODA-D [6] 包含24,828个高品质的流量场景图像,共有278,433个附加注释的9个类别实例. 培训、鉴定和测试子集被分成大约50%:20%:30%。 数据集包括高分辨的驱动场景,在不同的现实世界条件下,包括不同观点,天气,和发光等诸多小而极小的物体. 这些属性使得SODA-D成为了驱动情景中小物体检测的具有挑战性的基准.

blocks.en: D.1 Computational cost of high-resolution feature reuse
blocks.zh: D.1 高分辨率特性再利用的计算费用

blocks.en: Let N i N_{i} denote the number of tokens in P i P_{i} , and K K denote the number of sampling points. Standard global self attention for P i P_{i} and P i + 1 P_{i+1} has a complexity of 𝒪 ⁡ ( N i 2 ⋅ N i + 1 2 ) \mathcal{O}(N_{i}^{2}\cdot N_{i+1}^{2}) , while that in deformable self attention is 𝒪 ⁡ ( K ⋅ N i + K ⋅ N i + 1 ) \mathcal{O}(K\cdot N_{i}+K\cdot N_{i+1}) , which becomes expensive when the spatial resolution is large. In contrast, the complexity of our deformable interactions in CSDF is 𝒪 ⁡ ( K ⋅ N i + 1 ) \mathcal{O}(K\cdot N_{i+1}) , where K ≪ N i K\ll N_{i} , making the use of the highest-resolution feature P 1 P_{1} much more practical. Table 8 compares the computational cost of different ways to use the highest-resolution feature on DINO-4scale [ 52 ] . Directly adding raw C 1 C_{1} into the encoder and decoder causes a large cost increase, raising the whole-model GFLOPs from 354.4 to 3057.7. The main cost comes from the encoder, whose GFLOPs increase from 203.9 to 2709.5 due to dense interaction on the highest-resolution feature. The decoder cost also increases from 34.9 to 161.0. This is because each decoder layer performs value projection on the multi-scale memory, and the very large spatial size of C 1 C_{1} makes repeated projection expensive.

blocks.en:
In contrast, ReDHF increases the whole-model GFLOPs only to 407.8. Compared with direct C 1 C_{1} usage, ReDHF reduces the total computation by about 86.7%, the encoder computation by about 90.7%, and the decoder computation by about 74.7%.
This reduction comes from two designs. First, CSDF retrieves high-resolution details through sparse deformable interaction instead of dense global interaction. Second, FSQI exposes P 1 P_{1} to decoder cross-attention in a lightweight manner. In our implementation, the value projection for the highest-resolution feature is applied only once, while the remaining feature levels follow the original per-layer projection. Although FSQI allocates more sampling points to P 1 P_{1} , the total GFLOPs increase remains moderate, as shown in Fig. 5 . Moreover, EGSS is only used during training and removed during inference, so it does not add test-time computation. Overall, ReDHF is an efficient high-resolution detail reintroduction framework for tiny object detection. It avoids the expensive computational cost of utilizing raw C 1 C_{1} , while still effectively releasing the potential of the highest-resolution feature for tiny object detection.

这一减少来自于两个设计. 首先,CDF通过稀疏的可变形互动而不是密集的全球互动来取回高分辨率的细节. 第二,FSQI暴露出P 1 PQQ 1}以轻量级方式解码交叉注意. 在我们的实施中,最高分辨率特性的价值预测只应用一次,而其余特性水平则遵循原来的每层预测。 虽然FSQI为P1 P_{1}分配了更多的采样点,但如图5所示,GFLOP的总增长仍然中等. 此外,EGSS只在训练期间使用,在推论期间被去除,因此它不添加测试时间计算. 总体而言,ReDHF是用于微小物体探测的高效高分辨率细节再引入框架. 它避免了使用生的C 1 CQQ1}的昂贵计算成本,同时仍然有效地释放出微小物体探测最高分辨率特性的潜力.

blocks.en: As shown in Table 9 , increasing the input resolution of DINO-4scale from 800 to 864 raises the computation from 354.4 to 412.4 GFLOPs, but improves AP and AP vt by only 0.3 points. In contrast, ReDHF achieves 26.0 AP and 13.8 AP vt at 407.8 GFLOPs, outperforming the resolution-scaled baseline by 0.6 AP and 1.4 AP vt under a comparable computational budget. A similar trend is observed for Dome-DETR-L. These results indicate that the gains of ReDHF cannot be reproduced by uniformly increasing the input resolution, supporting the effectiveness of explicitly recovering and exploiting the discarded high-resolution representation.

blocks.en: Because ReDHF is designed primarily for tiny objects, we further examine whether recovering high-resolution evidence introduces a systematic trade-off at larger object scales. Table 11 summarizes the average gains over the five evaluated DETR variants, with the scale categories ordered from the smallest to larger objects for each dataset.
blocks.zh: 由于ReDHF主要是为微小物体设计的,我们进一步审查恢复高分辨率证据是否引入了较大物体尺度的系统取舍. 表11汇总了经评价的五个DETR变式的平均收益,每个数据集的尺度类别从最小对象到较大对象顺序。

blocks.en: The improvements are consistently largest on the smallest object categories and gradually decrease with object size. Nevertheless, the averaged gains on the remaining scales are non-negative across all three datasets. This indicates that ReDHF concentrates its benefits on objects most affected by feature downsampling without systematically sacrificing the detection quality of larger objects.

blocks.en: Appendix F Limitations Analysis
blocks.zh: 附录F 限制 分析

blocks.en: Retaining and querying an additional highest-resolution feature P 1 P_{1} inevitably introduces extra computation and memory compared with the original detectors. As quantified in Table 8 , however, this overhead is substantially smaller than that of directly incorporating the raw highest-resolution feature. More importantly, the additional cost is accompanied by consistent improvements in tiny-object detection, indicating a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off for exploiting high-resolution evidence.

blocks.en: As analysed in Sec. E , the benefits of ReDHF are concentrated on tiny objects, and the average improvement gradually decreases as object size increases, although no systematic degradation is observed at larger scales. This behavior is consistent with the motivation of ReDHF: high-resolution evidence is most useful for objects whose visual information is severely affected by feature downsampling. To identify where the occasional degradation on larger objects occurs, we divide the VisDrone validation set into two equally sized subsets according to the number of annotated instances per image and evaluate the same trained checkpoints on both subsets.

blocks.en: Table 14 compares different label assignment strategies for EGSS. The results show that the positive sample definition is important for shallow auxiliary supervision. Rectangle-based assignment reaches 33.2 AP, but its AP vt is 17.6. This suggests that using the whole box region as positives may introduce boundary background pixels, which is harmful for very tiny objects.

blocks.en: We further compare a short-axis circle-based strategy, where the positive region is a circle centered at the object center and its radius is set to the short semi-axis of the corresponding ground-truth box. This strategy reduces boundary noise and improves AP vt from 17.6 to 18.1, but it still ignores object aspect ratios and may discard valid positive regions along the long axis.

blocks.en: Table 16 compares different strategies for adapting P 1 P_{1} to the resolution of P 2 P_{2} in CSDF. The results show that simple fixed-rule downsampling is not always effective. Bilinear interpolation severely degrades performance, suggesting that directly resizing high-resolution responses may blur tiny-object details and introduce background interference. AvgPool and strided convolution perform better, but they still remain inferior to deformable cross-attention on the main metrics.

blocks.en: Deformable cross-attention achieves the best AP and AP vt . This is because it allows P 2 P_{2} to sparsely retrieve more relevant local responses from P 1 P_{1} . Rather than uniformly aggregating all nearby high-resolution signals, it can preserve more useful details for tiny object while reducing the redundant interferences of P 1 P_{1} more effectively. Although AvgPool obtains a slightly higher AP s , deformable cross-attention provides the best overall trade-off between accuracy and complexity, especially on very tiny objects. We therefore use deformable cross-attention as the default downsampling strategy for P 1 P_{1} in CSDF.

blocks.en: G.4 Sampling points in CSDF and FSQI
blocks.zh: G.4 CDF和FSQI的取样点

blocks.en: We further study the influence of sampling-point numbers in CSDF and FSQI, as shown in Fig. 5 . Both modules achieve the best performance with 8 sampling points, suggesting that sufficient sparse sampling is important for capturing fine-grained cues from the highest-resolution feature. However, further increasing the number of sampling points leads to noticeable drops in both AP and AP vt , indicating that overly dense sampling may introduce redundant or noisy responses from high-resolution features.
blocks.zh: 如图5所示,我们进一步研究取样点数对CDF和FSQI的影响。 这两个模块都以8个取样点达到最佳性能,表明足够稀有的取样对于从最高分辨率特性中捕取精细的提示非常重要。 然而,进一步增加取样点的数量导致AP和AP vt的明显下降,表明过于密集的取样可能带来高分辨率特性的多余或吵闹的反应。

blocks.en: The two modules also show different sensitivities to the sampling-point number. CSDF performs encoder-side detail injection from P 1 P_{1} to P 2 P_{2} , so the sampled responses are directly fused into the shallow feature. As a result, inappropriate sampling may more easily introduce background responses and disturb the feature representation. In contrast, FSQI exposes P 1 P_{1} to decoder queries through cross-attention, where each query can adaptively retrieve useful high-resolution responses together with information from other feature levels. This query-driven selection makes FSQI relatively more stable under different sampling settings, although excessive sampling is still harmful. Therefore, we set the number of sampling points to 8 for both CSDF and FSQI by default.
blocks.zh: 这两个模块还显示了对取样点数的不同敏感性。 CSDF执行从P 1 P_{1}到P 2 P_{2}的编码器-侧式细节注射,因此所抽样的响应被直接接入了浅层特征. 因此,不适当的采样可能更容易引入背景反应,并会干扰特征表述. 相形之下,FSQI让P 1 PQQ1}通过交叉调取来解码查询,其中每个查询可以适应性地检索有用的高分辨率回复以及来自其他特性级别的信息. 这种由查询驱动的选择使得FSQI在不同的采样设置下相对稳定,尽管过度采样仍然有害. 因此,我们默认将CDF和FSQI的抽样点数设定为8个.

blocks.en: G.6 Loss design in EGSS
blocks.zh: G.6 EGSS的损失设计

blocks.en: Table 19 studies the loss design of EGSS. The classification-only setting already achieves 33.2 AP, suggesting that foreground discrimination is essential for supervising the shallow feature. Adding a lightweight regression loss further improves AP to 33.5 and AP vt from 18.1 to 18.9, indicating that coarse localization guidance is helpful for very tiny objects. However, adding centerness supervision causes a clear drop to 32.1 AP and 15.8 AP vt . This suggests that centerness targets are unreliable on noisy shallow features, especially when tiny objects have only a few valid locations.
blocks.zh: 表19研究了EGSS的损失设计。 仅分类的设定已经实现了33.2 AP, 表明前景歧视对于监督浅层特征至关重要。 加上轻量级回归损失,AP进一步提高到33.5,AP vt从18.1到18.9,表明粗度定位指导对极小物体有帮助. 然而,增加中心监督导致32.1 AP和15.8 AP vt. 这表明中心目标在吵闹的浅层地物上是不可靠的,特别是在微小的物体只有几个有效的位置时.

blocks.en: We further vary the classification-regression weights. A small regression weight works better than a strong one: increasing λ reg \lambda_{\text{reg}} from 0.10 to 0.20 or 0.50 reduces AP vt from 18.9 to 17.6 and 17.3, respectively. Reducing the classification weight to 0.5 also degrades performance, showing that foreground classification should remain dominant in EGSS. Therefore, we use λ cls = 1.0 \lambda_{\text{cls}}=1.0 and λ reg = 0.10 \lambda_{\text{reg}}=0.10 by default, and omit centerness supervision.

blocks.en: To examine whether the degradation caused by centerness results from a particular loss weight, we vary λ ctr \lambda_{\mathrm{ctr}} from 0 to 0.10. As shown in Table 21 , the performance decreases monotonically as the centerness weight increases, with AP vt dropping from 18.9 without centerness to 18.0 and 15.8 at weights 0.05 and 0.10, respectively. We then analyze the sparsity of centerness targets across object scales as shown in Table 22 . Very tiny objects have only 1.90 positive locations on average, and 93.90% of them contain at most one location with a centerness target no smaller than 0.5. In comparison, the number of valid locations increases rapidly with object size. This analysis explains why explicit centerness supervision becomes excessively sparse and unstable for very tiny objects, supporting its exclusion from EGSS.
blocks.zh: 为了检查中心性引起的降解是否来自特定的损耗重量,我们从0.10到0.10不等。 如表21所示,由于中心重量增加,性能单调下降,在重量0.05和0.10时,AP vt分别从18.9无中心下降到18.0和15.8。 然后,我们分析表22所示各天体尺度的中心性指标的伸缩性。 极小的物体平均只有1.90个正方位,其中93.90%的物体最多含有一个中心目标不小于0.5的位置. 相较之下,有效位置的数量随对象大小而迅速增加. 这一分析解释了为什么对非常小的物体来说,明显的中心性监督变得过于稀少和不稳定,支持将其排除在环境商品和服务体系之外。

blocks.en: G.7 Robustness across random seeds

blocks.en:
1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide a detailed and accurate description of the paper’s contributions
and scope in both the abstract and introduction. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We discuss the limitations of ReDHF in Sec. 5 and Appendix F , including additional computational overhead, scale-dependent gains, and localized degradation for large objects in dense scenes. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not include theoretical results. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper provide the network architectures and hyperparameters required for the
experiments in Sec. 3 and Sec. 4.2 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The code are provided in the supplemental material. The data is public available and have been widely used. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide detailed descriptions of all the training and test details, including
backbones, hyperparameters, and training recipes in Sec. 4.2 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We report the mean and standard deviation across three random seeds for the full ReDHF model on AI-TOD-v2, as shown in Table 21 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide the hardware specifications required for the experiments. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The research conducted in the paper conform with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Our method significantly improves tiny object detection and can benefit applications such as remote sensing, traffic monitoring, and safety inspection. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Our method exclusively utilizes open-source models and datasets, ensuring that there is no risk of misuse. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Our method exclusively utilizes open-source models and datasets. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not release new assets. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This study does not involve any crowdsourced experiments or research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [N/A] Justification: The core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.

1. 联合国 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了该文件的贡献和范围? 答复: [是] 理由: 我们详细和准确地描述了该文件的贡献。
以及抽象和导言中的范围。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和/或导言应明确说明所提出的主张,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 [否]或[否/A]对这个问题的答复不会为审议者所看好。 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相匹配,并反映在多大程度上可以期望将结果归纳到其他环境中。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 说明: 我们讨论ReDHF在第5节和附录F中的局限性,包括额外的计算间接费用、依赖规模的收益和在密集场景中大型物体的局部退化。 • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反以及会产生什么影响。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果只在几个数据集上或用几个运行来测试这种做法。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社区完整性的准则方面起重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文不包括理论成果. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括理论结果. 二. 支助 纸上所有定理,公式和证明,都应该编号并相互参照. 二. 支助 • 所有假设均应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在正文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证明草图来提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 说明: 该文件提供了网络架构和超参数,以用于
3号和4.2号的实验 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大型语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 如补充材料所描述的那样,该文件是否提供了公开查阅数据和代码的机会,并提供了忠实复制主要实验结果的充分指示? 答复:[是] 说明: 守则载于补充材料。 这些数据是公开的,并已广泛使用。 · 答案[N/A]是指纸张不包括需要密码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 文件不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). 二. 支助 指令应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何取用原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本来复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从剧本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为了保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的资料(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(例如数据分解、超参数、如何选择、优化者类型等)? 答复:[是] 说明: 我们详细描述了所有培训和测试细节,包括:
骨干、超参数和4.2节的培训食谱。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 试验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便评估结果,使之有意义。 详细情况可通过守则、附录或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告的错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验的统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 如表21所示,我们报告AI-TOD-v2上完整的REDHF模型的三个随机种子的平均和标准偏差。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有出错栏、置信间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的可变因素(例如,列车/测试分拆、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算出错栏的方法应加以解释(封闭表单公式、调用库函数、靴子等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布式错误)。 应明确出错栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准出错. ^ 报告1-西格玛出错栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 撰文者最好报告2-相格马出错栏,而不是说如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,他们有96%的CI。 二. 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称错误栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负出错率). 二. 支助 如果在表格或图中报告出错栏,作者应在正文中解释其计算方式并参考正文中的相应数字或表格. 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 我们提供了实验所需的硬件规格. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额并估计总计算数。 文件应披露整个研究项目是否比文件所报道的实验需要更多的计算(例如,初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写入文件)。 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复: [是] 理由: 文件中进行的研究符合《新教IPS道德守则准则》: 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新教IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应当解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和负面社会影响? 答复:[是] 说明: 我们的方法大大改进了微小物体的探测,并有利于遥感、交通监测和安全检查等应用。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件不讨论社会影响。 二. 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(如:造谣、制造假相、监视)、公平考虑(如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多论文将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以使人们能训练出能更快生成Deepfake的模型. ^ 作者应考虑在技术被作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术被作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而可能造成的损害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行严格公布,在攻击之外提供防御,监测滥用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布滥用风险高的数据或模型(如预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或被刮去的数据集)而采取的保障措施? 答复:[是] 说明: 我们的方法专门使用开源模型和数据集,确保不会出现被滥用的风险。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放有可能被滥用或双重用途的已释放模型时,应采取必要的保障措施,允许控制地使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制进入模型或实施安全过滤器。 二. 支助 从互联网上取出的数据组可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明他们如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有者,是否适当记名,是否明确提到并适当遵守许可证和使用条件? 答复:[是] 说明: 我们的方法专门使用开源模型和数据集。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用了哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证的名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应当包括每项资产. 二. 支助 对于来自某一特定来源(例如网站)的报废数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产被放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于受欢迎的数据集,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 他们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 二. 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果不在网上提供这种信息,鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,与资产一起提供的文件是否充分? 答复:[不详]理由: 本文不放出新资产. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有释放出新的资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板通报数据集/代码/模型的细节,作为其提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 文件应讨论是否以及如何从资产被使用的人那里获得同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL , 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 与人类主题有关的众包和研究 关于与人类主体的众包实验和研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示和(如果适用的话)截图的全文,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 本研究不涉及任何与人类学科有关的众包式实验或研究. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人主体的研究. • 将这些资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人文主题,那么应在正文中尽可能详细。 二. 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少领取数据收集国的最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或等同的人类学科研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向研究对象披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得的同等批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文不涉及众包,也不涉及人类主体的研究. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人主体的研究. • 研究对象的研究可能需要IRB批准(或同等批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在文件中明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大相径庭,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 二. 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包含任何可能打破匿名性的信息(如果适用的话),例如进行审查的机构。 16. LLM使用宣言问题: 论文是否描述了LLMS的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作、编辑或格式化目的,而且不影响研究的核心方法、科学严谨性或原创性,则不需要申报。 答复:[不详]理由: 这一研究的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。 · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: We discuss the limitations of ReDHF in Sec. 5 and Appendix F , including additional computational overhead, scale-dependent gains, and localized degradation for large objects in dense scenes.
blocks.zh: 说明: 我们讨论ReDHF在第5节和附录F中的局限性,包括额外的计算间接费用、依赖规模的收益和在密集场景中大型物体的局部退化。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.
blocks.zh: • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反以及会产生什么影响。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果只在几个数据集上或用几个运行来测试这种做法。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社区完整性的准则方面起重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。

blocks.en: The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. blocks.en: While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility.
